title: gimp.appbundle install issues (in both user and system modes of "am")
body:
# Premise
"AM"/"AppMan" is just a tool to provide applications easily and quickly and is only responsible for integrating the AppImages into the system and installing the various programs available, respecting the following order (refer to the option "-d" to download the installation script without installing it):
- creation of the base directories and the removal script
- download of the package
- creation of the version file and the update script
- possibly, extraction of the icons and .desktop files, if needed

The malfunction of the installation scripts will then be taken into account. On the contrary, any malfunction related to individual applications is the responsibility of the related developer or packager. Refer to the option "-a" to know the sources of each program listed here, so you can contact them to report the bug.

--------------------------------------------------

## Please, describe the bug
I've been having issues with getting any appbundle working.  Here are my gimp woes.  First, with a "user" install ... seems to say it failed (and it does), then it seems quite happy (w/o the .desktop file, etc).
```
+ am install gimp.appbundle
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 "AM" is running as "AppMan", use am --system to switch it back to "AM"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
============================================================================

                  START OF ALL INSTALLATION PROCESSES

============================================================================

 ◆ "GIMP": starting installation script

gimp-3.0.4-github. 100%[================>] 127.98M  85.9MB/s    in 1.5s    
sed: can't read ./gimp.desktop: No such file or directory
mv: cannot stat './gimp.desktop': No such file or directory
 
 Oops! Something went wrong! Integrity check in progress... 

 "GIMP" INSTALLED (128 MB OF DISK SPACE)
____________________________________________________________________________
============================================================================

                  END OF ALL INSTALLATION PROCESSES

             The following new programs have been installed:

 ◆ gimp 3.0.4 

============================================================================

```



Then, in "system", the install goes OK, but running it is a bust (unlike gimp.am installed as root).  This is claude.ai's diagnosis:

###### Claude START
There's the problem! Look at the mount details for the GIMP AppImage:

dwarfs on /tmp/.pelfbundles/pbundle_orggimpGIMPgithubcompkgforgedevGIMPandPhotoGIMPAppImage304501_10_2025_b7ffbcc5/mounted type fuse.dwarfs (ro,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0)

The mounted filesystem has user_id=0,group_id=0 (root ownership), but you're running as user 1000 (joe). This is why you get "Permission denied" - the files are owned by root inside the mount.
Compare this to your working sas AppImage:

/home/joe/.appman/sas/sas on /tmp/.mount_sasremp11032738111699826672 type fuse.dwarfs (ro,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=1000,group_id=1000)


That one correctly has user_id=1000,group_id=1000.
The root cause: The GIMP AppImage is mounting with root ownership instead of your user ownership. This is likely a bug in how this particular AppImage handles FUSE mounts.
###### Claude END

Now, I don't know if that mean the appimage is internally flawed or the install of it is flawed (e.g., wrong permissions or something).  But, that is why I was trying to back off to the user one.

Anyhow, like I said, although I don't have many trials, appbundle's have not been kind to me.  Could be me.

title: Update install.am - add integrity check for broken download URLs
body:
The installation scripts include an `exit 1` that is executed if a URL download (via `wget`) fails.

This error is often due to temporary connection drops.

This change checks whether the "tmp" directory created during installation still exists, and if so, checks whether it is empty. If it is empty, up to 5 download attempts will be made, spaced 5 seconds apart.

In this example, I'm testing an installation script from a repository where the "latest" release doesn't exist, but only pre-releases, https://github.com/niess/python-appimage

During the process, I'll modify the running script (they run in ~/.cache/appman or ~/.cache/am, in my case I use `am -i --user`, so its a local installation, like AppMan) so that it will search for, find, and install the first generic release it finds.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a61fb6a2-842b-4faf-a76f-acdb258fc46f

This will also help me with false positives in https://github.com/ivan-hc/amcheck

title: Add "integrate" (alias --launcher) and "search" (alias -q)
body:
Some users are having trouble finding existing options.

This is the case with the option to integrate AppImages by dragging them into the terminal, `--launcher`, or the option to search for items in the list, `-q` or `query`.

This change adds `integrate` as an alias for `--launcher`, and `search` as an alias for `-q` or `query`.

Why didn't I do this before? I haven't received any reports of this before.

It was only recently pointed out to me that `--launcher` isn't intuitive, and the same seems to be true (on Reddit, by chance) for `-q` or `query`.

Let's put it this way: I, too, get confused when I have to install things on Arch Linux via Pacman or YAY: the word "install" doesn't start with an "S," but you need to install packages with `pacman -S packagename`. So I'm not the only one confusing people.

I hope this commit makes the user experience more "inclusive".

title: "AM" 9.9 - clone configurations and relocate AppMan apps
body:
fix https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM/issues/1817

Two new options added.

## Option `clone` or `--clone`
Clone your configuration and share it to other systems. Usage:
```
am clone
```
or
```
appman clone
```
this command without arguments only looks for a file named `am-clone.source`, on the Desktop first as prior path, then in the $HOME and then everywhere in the system, also on mounted devices.

Add the flag `-i` or `install` to also install the listed apps
```
am clone -i
```
or
```
appman clone -i
```

--------------------------------------

## Option `relocate` or `--relocate`
This option is for AppMan or for AM in AppMan mode and all AppMan apps (that can be managed also via AM).

As I explain on the README, AM installs everything always in /opt, by following the Linux Standard Base. That path will not be changed.

On the contrary, AppMan installs everything wherever you want, but you were unable to change the path once you have installed it and the apps.

Now you can
```
am relocate
```
or
```
appman relocate
```

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d1aee94-bcd4-4ac3-9ce5-35fde080cb03

title: fix `gpu-screen-recorder` not launching gui by default
[Known issue] The `-f` option is incredibly slow on reboot
body:
To reproduce the problem:
- reboot the system
- run `am -c` to clear the AM cache
- run `am -f`

You'll notice that the first boot is incredibly slow.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cb3e268-7966-4c9c-bc97-da51027fc8a6

## The cause
The culprit behind this problem is the `_files_if_appimage` function, in the "database.am" module.

https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM/blob/f886594da05e39780edc95b25d66a32230caeff9/modules/database.am#L247

This function not only marks the program as an "appimage," but also checks whether the AppImage
- is in a sandbox
- still depends on libfuse2

All these checks significantly slow down the process.

Until Anki 25.07, installing and updating with AppMan (e.g. `am install anki`) worked as expected.

Now, whether from an update or a totally fresh installation (including removal of `/home/[user]/.local/share/AnkiProgramFiles`), the following error message prohibits launch:

`Error: CopyFrom("/opt/anki/.python-version") "/home/[user]/.local/share/AnkiProgramFiles/.python-version": No such file or directory (os error 2)`

Upstream, 25.07.x has introduced a new special launcher with a new way to install and setup Anki:

https://github.com/ankitects/anki/releases/tag/25.07

25.07[.0] has been followed by 2 hotfix releases, so Anki is now on 25.07.2.

Presumably, the script for AM should be updated to use the new Anki mechanism for launch and installation.

title: Forkgram
body:
# Premise
"AM"/"AppMan" is just a tool to provide applications easily and quickly and is only responsible for integrating the AppImages into the system and installing the various programs available, respecting the following order (refer to the option "-d" to download the installation script without installing it):
- creation of the base directories and the removal script
- download of the package
- creation of the version file and the update script
- possibly, extraction of the icons and .desktop files, if needed

The malfunction of the installation scripts will then be taken into account. On the contrary, any malfunction related to individual applications is the responsibility of the related developer or packager. Refer to the option "-a" to know the sources of each program listed here, so you can contact them to report the bug.

--------------------------------------------------

## Please, describe the bug
Write here
Ciao Ivan, scrivo in italiano così riesco ad essere più esaustivo. C'è un problema nel'installazione di Forkgram. Lo script scarica il programma e crea il lanciatore forkgram che punta a forkgram, ma il programma non si avvia. Di fatto Telegram rimane chiuso in un archivio 7z con nome forkgram all'interno di /otp/forkgram. La soluzione semplice è estrarre manualmente Telegram dal contenitore in /otp/forkgram e correggere il lanciatore facendolo puntare a /otp/forkgram/Telegram. È possibile modificare lo script di installazione in questo senso. Grazie.
P.S.
Anche /usr/local/bin/forkgram è un archivio con all'interno Telegram.
